look_here_first: Start at the flower head, then move straight to the calyx. Purple prairie clover forms dense thimble-like to cylindrical heads; for the difficult D. purpurea versus D. compacta split, use calyx pubescence rather than flower color.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: perennial with stiff upright stems from a deep root

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: alternate odd-pinnate leaves with usually 3–7 very narrow leaflets

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dense thimble-shaped to cylindrical terminal flower heads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers progress upward on the head

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small legume with one or two seeds

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: calyx pubescence pattern is a priority character versus Dalea compacta

lookalikes.differences: D. compacta is the priority confuser: D. compacta has calyx hairs arranged in longitudinal lines separated by bald areas, while D. purpurea has hairs distributed over the calyx-tube surface. D. enneandra has a loose spike with exposed rachis; D. tenuis is consistently 3-foliolate with extremely narrow leaflets.
